question.text: If a call option has delta = 0.45, gamma = 0.05, and the underlying moves up by Rs 3, what is the approximate new delta?

answer.text: 0.60 (New delta = Old delta + Gamma × Price change = 0.45 + 0.05 × 3 = 0.60)

explanation.text: The Logic: Gamma is the change in delta per unit change in the underlying. New delta = Old delta + Gamma × Price change = 0.45 + 0.05 × 3 = 0.60. The Trap: 0.50 adds gamma only once instead of multiplying by the price change. 0.48 uses an incorrect formula. 1.35 multiplies delta by the price change. Note: Delta-neutral portfolios must be rebalanced as delta changes; this is why delta hedges are adjusted as the underlying moves.
